context.in_practice: If a line already has a quoting style that can hold the new value, the line keeps that style. If it can't, the tool picks a different style: a `yes-ish` line set to the text `true` gets single quotes. A new key whose value contains an emoji also got single quotes, even though unquoted comes first in the fallback order. One arm changed how it decides which characters count as printable (non-breaking space, emoji) after review. In these runs all six arms produced the same file.
context.stakes: When you set a value, the tool decides how it is quoted in troupe.yml. That decides whether the file stays the way you wrote it, and whether a value like `true` comes back as text or as a yes/no flag.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 keeps your file's existing quoting wherever it can. In exchange, a value can be written differently depending on which line it lands on, for example a real tab inside single quotes.

plan_why: Shows which quoting style each change gets: an existing single-quoted value given an emoji, a plain value given a no-break space (U+00A0), a plain value given the string 'true' (plain cannot hold it, so single is next), a single-quoted value given a TAB (single quotes can hold it), and a new key copying its sibling's single quotes with an emoji value. Implementations with a wrong printable check fall back to double quotes or escapes here.
routes: Keep the existing style if it can hold the value; otherwise plain, then single, then double
